title: Slot tenure optimizer for interleaved short/long prompts and KV residency tuning
creator: Marco Li
description: Problem: Production traffic often mixes very short user prompts (single-turn queries, <50 tokens) with long multi-turn generations (>1k tokens). Continuous batching currently favors maximizing GPU utilization which increases tail latency and causes KV cache churn: short sessions occupy slots briefly but cause fragmented KV residency and premature eviction of long-dialogue caches. Goal: tune slot allocation, KV residency (tenure), and preemption policies so short/long interleaved workloads achieve predictable P95 latency and lower per-token cost without large regressions to P50 throughput. This ticket scopes experiments, implementation, and rollout for a slot-tenure optimizer that adapts KV residency and slot coalescing heuristics based on live sequence-length histograms and per-route SLAs.
success_criteria: P95 generation latency for short prompts <= 120ms at 95th percentile load
P95 token latency for long responses decreases by >= 10% or remains within 5% of baseline
KV hit rate uplift +6 percentage points for mixed traffic workloads
GPU memory fragmentation index reduced by 12% under synthetic skewed traffic
No customer-facing errors or increased OOM incidents during canary rollout
work_items: Implement slot-tenure policy: assign short-slot TTL and long-slot pinning with adjustable KV tenure
Add telemetry: per-slot sequence-length histogram, KV residency time, eviction reason tags
Create adaptive preemption: allow short-slot coalescing into transient micro-slots and controlled preemption of idle long slots
Extend autoscaler hints: surface tenure pressure to scheduler to trigger targeted warmups
Run synthetic experiments covering 80/20, 50/50, and 20/80 short:long mixes with 4 GPU sizes
Integrate into canary pipeline and add rollback guards (error budget thresholds and OOM alarms)
decision_log: 2026-02-27: Chose slot-tenure approach over aggressive binning to avoid hard reclassification during streaming responses
2026-03-02: Use KV tenure measured in seconds (configurable) rather than slot-count touch due to cross-GPU eviction semantics
2026-03-05: Telemetry standard will include 'eviction_reason' labels to disambiguate kv-eviction vs slab-reclaim
2026-03-10: Canary rollout will start in us-west-2 with 5% traffic and automatic rollback on >2% error increase
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike implemented: prototype slot-tenure policy in local dev cluster; validated no binary size change
2026-03-01: Added extra metrics to runtime: per-slot liveliness and kv_residency_seconds (in internal metrics registry)
2026-03-04: Initial synthetic run (80% short, 20% long) showed +8% KV hit but P95 short latency regressed—identified coalescing window too large
2026-03-08: Tuned coalescing window from 15ms -> 6ms; P95 short latency recovered, long-response throughput improved slightly
2026-03-11: End-to-end bench with 4xA100 equivalent shows GPU fragmentation index down 9% and KV hit +4pt; preparing canary PR
risks: Incorrect tenure settings can worsen long-dialogue tail latency by pinning memory to dead slots
Telemetry cardinality growth if we add too many per-slot labels — could inflate ingest costs
Edge cases: streaming tokens that escalate from short->long mid-request; need careful reclassification to avoid double-residency
Interference with Dedicated customers that have strict memory reservations; will require per-tenant opt-out
test_plan: Unit tests for tenure state machine (expiry, refresh-on-access, forced-pin)
Integration tests: run continuous-batcher with synthetic workload generator (short/long mixes) and assert KV hit behavior
Load test: multi-GPU cluster with synthetic skewed dialogs to measure fragmentation and slot churn
Chaos test: inject delayed eviction metrics and simulate OOM scenarios to verify rollback
Customer scenario test: replay sampled production traces (anonymized) on staging to validate no regression
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge feature gated behind runtime flag + extensive e2e tests
Stage 1 (Canary): Enable for 5% traffic in us-west-2 for 48 hours; monitor P95, error-rate, OOM alarms
Stage 2 (Gradual ramp): 5% -> 25% -> 60% in 24h increments observing metrics and manual sign-off
Stage 3: Global rollout with per-tenant opt-out for Dedicated/private customers
Rollback criteria: >2% absolute error increase, >8% P95 degradation vs baseline, any OOM incident
